extracted.intended_audience: intellectuals, scholars, cultural critics, and policymakers concerned with technology, media, and democracy
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive and critical guidance for intellectuals and scholars about how to respond to, interpret, and influence the social and political consequences of electronic media and technological change. It outlines what intellectuals should avoid doing (e.g., myth-making, utopian planning, neo-Luddite spectacle) and what constructive actions they should pursue (e.g., demythologizing rhetoric, cultivating arts/ethics/politics, and enabling democratic discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Against convoking grand futurist projects
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not the convocation of a Vision ’80, a Mankind 2000 project, or a congress of futurologists; intellectual involvement in elaboration of plans for the application of technology has been an inadequate approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical experience shows such planning-focused intellectual projects fail because the bias of electronic power is antithetical to dispersed use and small-scale control. Avoid treating large futurist spectacles as substitutes for concrete political and cultural work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid complicity in myth‑making of the electrical complex
rubrics_metrics.description: The promotion of the illusion of an 'electronic revolution' borders on complicity by intellectuals in the myth-making of the electrical complex itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not celebrate electronics in ways that contribute to cults of engineering, mobility, and fashion; such celebration sacrifices roots, tradition, and political organization and obscures real social problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demythologize the rhetoric of the electronic sublime
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronics is neither the arrival of apocalypse nor the dispensation of grace. Technology is technology; it is a means for communication and transportation over space, and nothing more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismantle rhetorical fetishes of technology and of 'communication for the sake of communication.' Emphasize content, context, and realistic appraisal over romanticized or apocalyptic narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curtail the influence of technics and cultivate arts, ethics, and politics
rubrics_metrics.description: The demise of culture could be offset only by a deliberate curtailment of the influence of technics and those institutions in which technics were encased and by a strenuous cultivation of the realms of art, ethics, and politics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take active measures—political, scholarly, and cultural—to counterbalance technological bias; favor qualitative cultural checks (art, ethics, politics) rather than only quantitative measures of 'quality of life.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Address uprooting and organize around authentic political issues
rubrics_metrics.description: We should address ourselves directly to the overriding problems: the uprooting of people from meaningful communities and the failure to organize politically around authentic issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that functional participation and geographic decentralization alone cannot solve constitutional/governance problems; prioritize democratization and reconciling concentrated power and wealth with ideals of liberty and equality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate scholarly relevance through accessible critical studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectuals should demonstrate the relevance of scholarly integrity and rationality by critical studies that can reach an audience in sympathetic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate scholarship in language and formats that secure public hearing; focus on positive values (arts, ethics, politics) rather than purely negativistic critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure a democratic vocabulary linking words to political objects
rubrics_metrics.description: That hearing must be secured in a language of democracy... in which political words are again joined to political objects and processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuild a public political vocabulary that connects discourse to concrete institutions and actions—support formation of a 'party of the mind' to restore democratic discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject neo‑Luddite spectacle and symbolic protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Neo-Luddite activities (Orwellian science fiction, symbolic 'wounding the Pentagon,' electric circuses) are forms of escapism that merely Americanize the myth and fail to offer alternative ways of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid protest forms that are only symbolic or theatrical; they produce a debilitating sense of powerlessness and do not yield practical alternatives or political organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on purely literary or isolated strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: The electronic revolution cannot be managed by purely literary strategies, by creating images of the antisublime, or by creating new zones of romantic isolation and innocence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary or utopian isolationism is inadequate; combine cultural critique with sustained political and scholarly work that addresses real-world institutions and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control the bias of technology through politics and democratic avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: The bias of technology can be controlled only by politics, by curtailing the expansionist tendencies of technological societies and by creating avenues of democratic discussion and participation beyond the control of modern technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use political mechanisms—regulation, public policy, institutional design—to limit expansionist/centralizing tendencies and to open participatory channels not mediated solely by centralized electronic media. Be pragmatically open to formal centralism when needed to secure democratic ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve stability and the oral tradition as countervailing culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the oral tradition, with its emphasis on dialogue and dialectic, values and philosophical speculation, as the countervailing culture to the technological culture of sensation and mobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and extend elements of permanence: communities of association and styles of life protected from relentless technical obsolescence; foster cultural enclaves that sustain dialogue and deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate communications media by capacity for participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern media widen the range of reception while narrowing the range of distribution. Large audiences receive but are unable to make direct response or participate otherwise in vigorous discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess media not only on reach but on the extent to which they permit direct response, dialogue, and civic participation; design or reform systems to enable genuine two-way deliberation rather than one-way administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not equate technical projects with democratic outcomes (TVA caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TVA experience demonstrates the folly of identifying technical projects with the creation of democratic community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate technological initiatives (dams, electrification, etc.) for their social, ecological, and political consequences rather than accepting rhetorical claims that they will automatically produce decentralization, democracy, or social renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist monopolies and cultural imperialism in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Monopolies of communication (whether of electrical technology or rigid orthodoxy) are threats to human freedom and cultural survival; electronic media can increase capacities for imperialism and cultural invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppose entrenched communication monopolies through scholarship, politics, and institutional alternatives; attend to international frequency allocation, industry concentration, and cultural consequences of exported technology.
